name: Symmetric successive relaxation sweep
variables: A symmetric matrix; D,L,U splitting; ω fixed relaxation; y forward sweep
assumptions: Real symmetric positive definite A, nonzero diagonal, 0<ω<2, fixed ordering, finite-precision residual checks and bounded iterations.
limitations: Two sequential sweeps; not necessarily faster than forward SOR.
failure_conditions: Zero diagonal, invalid relaxation or residual stagnation
computation: Apply forward and reversed relaxed triangular sweeps; check true residual.

source.citation: Barrett et al., Templates for the Solution of Linear Systems, §2.2.4, equation (2.9); signs translated to A=D+L+U. https://netlib.org/templates/templates.html

required_inputs: Symmetric matrix, right side, initial iterate, relaxation, stop criteria.
incompatible_methods: Treating two sweeps as independently validated evidence
mechanism_note: Forward SOR followed by a reverse-order SOR sweep changes the iteration operator and is a material SOR variant. It is not a new distinct algorithm or independent evidence.

name: Chebyshev polynomial linear iteration
definition: For real SPD A with eigenvalues enclosed by [a,h], 0<a<h, set d=(a+h)/2, c=(h−a)/2, t=d/c, r_k=b−Ax_k. Set x₁=x₀+r₀/d and ρ₁=1/t. For k≥1 set ρ_(k+1)=1/(2t−ρ_k), α_k=2ρ_(k+1)/c, β_k=ρ_(k+1)ρ_k, x_(k+1)=x_k+α_k r_k+β_k(x_k−x_(k−1)). In exact arithmetic e_k=T_k((dI−A)/c)e₀/T_k(t).
variables: a,h spectral bounds; b right-hand side; d,c interval center and half-width; ρ normalization ratio; e_k=x_k−x*; T_k first-kind Chebyshev polynomial
assumptions: Real SPD operator, valid finite positive enclosing spectral interval of nonzero width, safe scalar arithmetic, explicit residual tolerance and iteration bound.
limitations: Poor bounds degrade convergence; no guarantee for general nonsymmetric matrices.
failure_conditions: Invalid interval, nonfinite recurrence or residual tolerance failure
computation: Start by checking the initial true residual; compute normalized scalar ratios, matrix-vector products and two-vector recurrence; stop on true residual tolerance or declared failure. No exact solution is required.

source.citation: Eric Darve, Numerical Linear Algebra, The Chebyshev Iteration Method, normalized minimax polynomial and Chebyshev recurrence; ratio form obtained algebraically from the polynomial normalization. https://ericdarve.github.io/NLA/content/chebyshev_acceleration.html

required_inputs: Operator, right side, initial vector, spectral bounds, stopping criteria.
incompatible_methods: Using unverified spectral bounds as guaranteed
mechanism_note: Spectral-bound-dependent varying coefficients yield a predetermined minimax error polynomial, unlike constant-step gradient descent, adaptive CG or FISTA extrapolation. Not independent empirical evidence.
